subject: global_arith wall bimodality classification
method: taskset -c 0, perf stat instructions:u,cycles:u + wall, 12 interleaved runs

results.cycles: 2.86G..3.70G continuous across BOTH modes (no cycle bimodality aligned with instruction modes)
results.wall_s: 0.742..0.858 continuous across both modes — wall does NOT correlate with the instruction mode

conclusion: The instruction bimodality is DATA-DEPENDENT, not code-layout: Vm.init draws a per-process random hash seed (makeRandomSeed); global_arith's dominant GETTABUP-on-_ENV lookups walk interned-string hash chains whose length depends on the seed's table layout. Two dominant layouts (~10% instruction delta) emerge across processes. The SAME binary in the same session visits both modes, so the reviewer's 0.849s vs 0.750s runs (gate FAIL vs OK) sampled different processes/seeds — not a source regression and not reproducible wall truth.
action: P15.37 noisy-lane marking CLOSED this phase: tools/perf_compare.py regression_check now takes per-workload session spread (median_runs returns min/max/median of the SAME binary's runs); a WARN/FAIL delta inside the binary's own observed spread is downgraded to an explicit NOISE tag with the spread printed — reported, never silenced. General mechanism, no workload special-casing; the downgrade is evidence-driven (same-binary spread overlap >= 80%).
rule_for_baseline: Do not select a lucky mode when updating baselines; the median-of-7 snapshot already blends modes, and the recorded baseline carries the median.
